title: backlog.py stage-back ID copies a headless worker's .claude/ staging copies into its worktree, checks and commits them
goal: Retrospective of SP-sbdy4hsx: every code story touched .claude/ files, so the orchestrator copied each worker's staging copies back by hand (13 files over 4 items), ran selfdoc.py check and the item's checks there, and wrote a second commit with Self-Reviewed for each. backlog.py stage-back ID copies the staging copies dispatch named into the worker's worktree, refuses a copy whose base differs from the worktree's file, runs selfdoc.py check and the item's own checks there, and commits the copies alone with KB-Work on work/ID; the kb-sprint skill's run step 3 names it; a test stages a planted copy and finds one new commit holding only it.
notes: SP-etslk6yu close evidence: ST-f2n2h22c's kb-census and kb-refresh SKILL.md staging copies were copied back, checked and committed by hand once more.
